- the agenda calls for statements by the council and the commission on the progress report on the intergovernmental conference.
the council. - mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, i am pleased to present to this house the state of progress of the process of constitutional reform of the european union. the italian presidency is convinced that only with the support of the european parliament will it be possible to solve the many problems we are facing and to reach a political agreement in december. for this reason, and in line with the traditional italian position, we have fought to extend the european parliament's participation in the work of the intergovernmental conference as far as possible. the convention on the future of europe has been an innovative way of starting the current process of reforming the treaties. the draft treaty that it drew up was not the result of a simple intergovernmental confrontation, but was shaped by constructive contributions and a structured, comprehensive, public and transparent debate on the future of europe, which for the first time in the history of the european integration process actively involved national parliaments and representatives of civil society. the political value of the success achieved must therefore not be dissipated or weakened by the work of the igc. the latter, on the contrary, has the task of improving and supplementing those parts of the treaty on which there is not yet full agreement. any other solution would be interpreted as an attempt to weaken the democratic and transparent method which was undertaken with the work of the european convention. if that were the case, it would be a step backwards which our fellow citizens would find it difficult to understand and justify. this approach is the basis for the main objective of the italian presidency: to reach a comprehensive political agreement on the constitutional text as early as december. this will make it possible to sign the future constitutional treaty - a constitution for europe, as defined by president giscard d'estaing - in the period between 1 may 2004, the date foreseen for the entry of the ten new member states, and the election of the european parliament. beyond that date, a prolongation of the constitutional negotiations would entail two serious problems of legitimacy and democratic transparency: on the one hand, there would be a gradual dispersion of the convention's constituent heritage and, on the other, european citizens would vote for the elections to the european parliament, ignoring the constitutional characteristics of the future europe. the need to find consensual solutions to the still controversial issues will not in any case encourage the italian presidency to negotiate a 'cheap' compromise which would involve significant steps backwards from the convention's proposals. our aim is to achieve a high-quality result that meets the expectations of european citizens and is capable of guaranteeing the efficient and democratic functioning of the union in the future. giving the european union a constitution is a challenge, not just for some countries or for the italian presidency, which has the honour of guiding the council during this phase, but a challenge for all. we owe it to our fellow citizens: if we do not meet this challenge, a united europe is a loser, the union is a loser as a factor of stability and prosperity on the world stage, and we are all losers. after the opening ceremony on 4 october, the igc's work went straight to the heart of the matter. in this context, institutional issues appear, as was to be expected, to be by far the most complex. the most important issues concern the composition of the commission, the procedures for electing and the powers of the president of the european council, the status of the minister for foreign affairs and the calculation of the qualified majority. these themes were further developed during the igc sessions held in the first half of october. the ministerial meeting on 27 october broadened the range of analyses to include issues not covered or only marginally covered at previous meetings. the following subjects were discussed in particular: the presidency of council configurations; the extension of qualified majority voting; and non-institutional matters, particularly as regards economic and financial provisions. the debate confirmed the existence of differentiated positions among the member states and the essentially balanced nature of the proposals contained in the draft constitutional treaty approved by the convention. it has become clear that the reopening of the discussion on certain specific aspects of the convention text leads to the repetition of opposing proposals and does not foreshadow new forms of consensus. the results of the work of this session allow the following conclusions to be drawn. firstly, there is a gradual convergence of views on the future presidency of the council formations, even if this subject will have to be re-examined in the context of a comprehensive proposal on all the institutional systems of the future enlarged union. the vast majority of states are opposed to the establishment of a council for legislative affairs. the presidency takes note of this opposition but will try to do everything possible to ensure that the council for legislative affairs is retained in the treaty, at least as an option, as a possible evolution of the system of councils. secondly, they confirm that the member states still have divergent positions on the issue of the scope of qualified majority voting. in the light of this situation, the presidency will consider ways of finding consensual solutions - especially in sensitive and key areas such as taxation, own resources, judicial cooperation in criminal matters and police cooperation - while remaining aware that the draft convention remains the main basis for building a balanced and ambitious agreement. thirdly, the provision of a manifestly excessive number of other non-institutional themes by the member states was clearly incompatible with the igc timetable, which was developed in thessaloniki and confirmed in brussels by the heads of state or government. the presidency will then proceed to examine this group of topics on the basis of a selective approach, identifying those areas where an alternative consensus to the draft convention appears to be emerging and those requiring technical and drafting clarifications. it will then be for the member states to decide whether they wish to insist on specific and minority points by bringing the matter, if necessary, to the attention of the heads of state or government. based on the draft convention and the work of the foreign ministers, the presidency will develop a comprehensive proposal focusing on the institutional package and defence, which will try to take into account the requirements of the member states, the acceding states and the candidate countries. this proposal will in any case start from the draft convention and aim to achieve compromises at least as ambitious and noble as those proposed by the convention. we are willing to consider possible adaptations, but equally resolutely opposed to upheavals and setbacks. the outcome of these negotiations is very likely to determine the future of the european constitution. therefore, and given the importance of the issue, the approach to these constitutional negotiations will have to be characterised by a good margin of flexibility on the part of all the actors called upon to lay the foundations of the union of the 21st century. we must abandon particularism and the logic of fair profit, according to which every concession must be equal to the cost incurred. this approach is - or rather would be - contrary to the very concept of european integration and, if systematically applied, would risk undermining the foundations of the union. although fairness is an essential condition for any constitutional pact, no one can put a brake on the current evolution of the integration process. those who wish to do so will have to take responsibility before history, before their european partners and, above all, before their fellow citizens. the approval of the new constitution will be a success for all or a failure for the union. there can be no essential opposition between the national interest and the european interest. (applause) i would like to thank
president and rapporteur for the opinion of the committee on budgets. - mr president, mr méndez de vigo called me last week to inform me of the ecofin proposals and mr hänsch came to our committee on monday. on both occasions, i was completely amazed by what they told us. i cannot believe that the council is adopting ecofin's proposals in the budgetary field. as a british citizen, i can understand why he is acting in this way on the question of own resources. whether he's right is another matter. on the other two questions, the financial perspective and the budgetary procedure, he is out of line. such an action would neutralize this parliament. there would be no need for a committee on budgets if this proposal were adopted by the igc. i'll tell you frankly, we'd be emasculated with a pair of rusty scissors. we have no need for this kind of 'domination' of the council. parliament has already lost a lot of weight in trying to reach agreement within the convention - and the council says it has done the same. we have nevertheless agreed that the financial perspective should be included in the treaty. now, if the interinstitutional agreement is broken, we go back to the treaty, which gives parliament much more power and authority. we sacrificed that element in order to make a deal, which is a more cooperative approach and would mean that we cooperate, that we work together. however, we are not dealing with cooperation, but with coercion on the part of the council. we cannot allow things to continue as they are and we must do everything possible to ensure that this does not happen. - (pt) mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, we can only speak of progress in the work of the intergovernmental conference with irony or humour. did not rabelais say that laughter is the property of man? in writing. - it is very good to want to eliminate discrimination in electoral candidates, as proposed in the dybkjær report, but it is even better not to add any. the french law of 11 april 2003, which makes the voting system for the european elections regional, clearly disadvantages small-medium parties. in these circumstances, it can be argued that the law infringes the decision of the european council of ministers of 25 june 2002 that, when a european election taking place in a single national constituency is regionalised - as is the case in france - the reform must be carried out 'without overall affecting the proportionality of the electoral system'. the strangest thing is that the 2002 european decision was adopted by france, in accordance with article 190 (4) of the treaty, by a law passed only on 16 october 2003. in other words, the correct procedure would now be to adapt the french law of april to the european decision approved in october! unfortunately, it must also be noted that there is nothing to remove such a contradiction between national law and community law.
in writing. - the fact that we voted against this report cannot, of course, be interpreted as any manifestation of hostility towards the representation of women in politics. apart from the fact that the general philosophy of the report - positive discrimination - is contrary to the constitutional traditions of certain member states, and in particular to the republican universalism on which french law is based, the rejection of this text is based solely on respect for the distribution of competences between the union and the member states. in this case, in the absence of a uniform electoral procedure, the european union has no competence to intervene, as this report calls for, in the definition of the rules governing the organisation of the european elections. consequently, the european parliament cannot validly ask national political parties to introduce 'quota systems, such as the system of alternating the two sexes on the lists called the 'snap-closure' system and/or to take measures to encourage balanced participation', nor to ask the commission to disseminate information 'on the concept of equal democracy' ('), nor to call for 'the funding of awareness-raising campaigns' on the subject.
in writing. - we voted against the sanders-ten holte report on the so-called 'cooperation of the community with the countries of asia and latin america', with the exception of a few amendments on humanitarian aid, hoping that this will not be lost in the sands of the corruption of local political leaders. in our view, the amount of aid is paltry. it is enough to note, as we denounce, that when aid to latin america is supposed to be increased, aid to asia is reduced. this aid is a mere sprinkling of water, and it is not able to erase the tragic consequences of the pillage which has always been carried out by large european and north american companies or financial institutions in these regions and in others. by seizing raw materials at low prices, by cutting off areas of influence or by charging high prices for their services, the greed of the big european companies, combined with that of their local friends, is the very source of the impoverishment of the populations of these continents. in recent years, this has even led to the collapse of several national economies on these two continents. the european union's economic guidelines, far from eradicating poverty, are only increasing it.
in writing. - better coordination of national taxation of motor vehicles may seem necessary, but this should not be the occasion for the introduction of a european taxation. this taxation of private cars cannot be separated from a general tax system involving vat, income or corporation tax, excise duties, which is also an instrument of budget revenue and must as such be the responsibility of the sovereignty of the states. the environmental angle chosen by the european commission does not suit me either. taxing passenger cars at european level, as proposed, does not seem to me appropriate, firstly because many more polluting sectors are not affected because of strong lobbying and secondly because the structure of the car market is specific to each state. small and large countries, flat and mountainous countries, countries with a weak road infrastructure, countries with a strong tradition of public transport, etc. are all differences which are specific to each state and cannot be levelled out all at once by a harmonised taxation of passenger cars. - madam president, i shall stick to one point: is there a need for a european telecommunications regulation? nick clegg says, "it must only be temporary". i say: "it must be permanent and more solid than the current regulation". i would have liked nick to have taken better account of the analyses of leading oxford and cambridge economists, who point out that, while competition policy acts ex post, regulation is necessary ex ante to meet economic, social and ecological objectives. the rapporteur stresses that the incumbent operators must give way to competition. yes, but it will not automatically be efficient, or even effective, in an oligopoly situation. the european telecoms sector has just gone through a beresina in terms of investment and jobs and has lost its lead with the gsm standard. a regulation for the umts would have allowed for the sharing of infrastructure use, instead of investors duplicating it by taking on heavy debt. secondly, the contradiction between the 'price' and the 'quality' criteria forced the uk regulator to impose higher quality obligations on british telecom. the commission's report on the social and territorial cohesion objective is particularly weak. is there really a universal access? commission. – mr president, the commission welcomes the outcome of the conciliation process and is pleased that the co-legislators decided not only to broaden the scope of the seveso ii directive in the light of the accidents in baia mare, enschede and toulouse, but also to strengthen its provisions. the new directive now covers chemical and thermal processing operations in mining as well as all operational tailings disposal facilities containing dangerous mining waste. furthermore, its scope was tightened with regard to explosive and pyrotechnic substances as well as ammonium nitrate. taking into account the results of two studies carried out by the commission, the directive also includes more carcinogenic substances, and the qualifying quantities for substances toxic to the aquatic environment have been significantly decreased. moreover, and particularly due to requests by the european parliament, the directive has now been strengthened in a number of other areas such as information for the public, training for emergencies and the involvement of subcontracted personnel. its provisions on land-use planning were reinforced, including a mandate for the commission to develop a european database to be used for assessing the compatibility between seveso establishments and sensitive areas. the new directive now also obliges industrial operators to produce risk maps showing areas that might be affected by a major accidents. last, but not least, member states are required to provide the commission with minimum data on all seveso sites on their territory. i would like to congratulate mr lisi, the rapporteur, on his work, as well as all members who have contributed to ensuring the successful outcome of this legislative process.

as mr wurtz alluded to, you were aware of this - more and more directly against europe in order to challenge the very foundations of european construction, as was seen with this european social forum which, personally, i would have renamed the 'european sovereignist forum' in view of the debates held there. finally, we could talk a lot about the bridges, which are in fact dark tunnels, where the last prerogatives of national democracies are going to be lost. but i would like to refer to an incident that took place yesterday to show this parliament just a little bit how schizophrenic it can be from time to time. one group, the largest in our institution, has attacked mr prodi for his involvement in italian politics, and this is happening at a time when all the representatives of this parliament have been fighting during the convention to ensure that the president of the commission is elected by parliament and that it is therefore possible to campaign. i remember this question being raised several times. it would be so interesting to campaign for prodi or aznar in the european elections! mr prodi yesterday merely anticipated a decision which i regard as regrettable, namely the politicization of the office of president of the commission.
- mr president, the meeting of the igc foreign ministers on 18 november dealt in particular with a very important problem which the convention had never really discussed: the clauses for revising the draft european constitution. some suggested moving towards a relaxation of the unanimity requirement for certain revisions, notably the one on the third part of the draft, the one on union policies. such majority revisions are unacceptable because they would impose changes to the constitutional pact on minority peoples. unanimity must be maintained and differentiated cooperation must respond to possible deadlock situations. i would also like to point out in passing that this third part contains essential provisions; that it has hardly been considered by the convention and that the intergovernmental conference is about to follow the same path. all this shows that this titanic ambition to rewrite all the treaties at once risks leading to the approval of contested policies without a genuine democratic debate. the meeting of foreign ministers also examined the many individual and general closures which abound in the project. we reject these bridge clauses which are designed to circumvent the formal review procedure, which will exclude the national parliaments from the procedure and which will make it even less transparent to the citizens. of course, this would not be the case if each national parliament considered separately, or each people by referendum, had a formal right of opposition. mr president, the aim of this new revision of the treaties should have been to close the democratic deficit, to bring europe closer to the citizens and to enhance the role of the national parliaments. the intergovernmental conference is not moving in this direction, however, since it is tending to adopt the draft convention as a whole, which does not address the real problem of democracy and which even distances europe from its peoples. we call on the commission to set the bar again: there is still time before the compromise of 28 november.

in writing. - in matters of security, there can be no derogation, no lax tolerance. we must get shipping out of the profit maximisation laws and create another international maritime organisation which is able to respect social needs, workers and the environment. we need more regulations, more coercive international laws and the abolition of the complaisance system. the prestige oil tanker disaster, which occurred just a year ago, and its human, social and environmental consequences remind us every day, from a coruña to calais, of these needs. my priority in this area is not the fight against terrorism, but the fight against sea bandits. i supported all the amendments to include in the regulation the strengthening of security measures in community ports, to cover all the personnel concerned, not only seafarers but also all professionals working occasionally in port areas and to extend the scope of the regulation to vessels carrying containers, petroleum products and dangerous goods. for these reasons, i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - the office which the council is preparing to set up is responsible for 'network and information security'. its initiators are mainly concerned with what they call the 'business world' and the protection of this small world against 'computer crime'. some elements of the so-called business world are likely to have financial implications from this case as the agency will use their it security service. we are of course in favour of improved computer security. but since the protection of business secrets in relations between private companies is not one of our concerns, we abstained.

in writing. - the commission proposes to finance research on embryonic stem cells despite the opposition of some member states who prohibit it, and also in defiance of the principle of subsidiarity. research on embryonic stem cells, which automatically leads to the destruction of the embryo, is totally contrary to the principle of human dignity recognised by the charter of fundamental rights (article 2). this research also raises technical problems: we are not yet looking at it for therapeutic purposes. so when it comes to basic research, there is no justification for using new embryos: this is peter liese's compromise. very few of us spoke about the suffering of the sick and the need to find emergency therapies. this is the question that stem cell research is asking. at the present stage of research, only the use of adult stem cells is promising. it is not ethical or technical, but unfortunately it lacks the financial means. this is why the bulk of european funding should be devoted to this type of research, which alone can meet the urgent demands of patients. for all these reasons, i will support the gargani amendments which i co-signed.

the commission. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i should like to thank mr queiró for his excellent report on the commission communication on defence industry and market issues. in its resolution of april 2002, the european parliament called on the commission to address industry and market issues in the european defence industry. the development of events in recent years, as exemplified by the gradual structuring of european security and defence policy, and the changes in the industry itself have set the stage for a reassessment of the question, which a few years ago was considered premature. the commission is fully aware of the sensitivity of this area and the specific nature of the defence sector. we have therefore taken a cautious approach, stressing the prospects for the development of europe's industrial and technological potential in the long term and indicating that the commission is determined to contribute substantially to the european union's efforts wherever possible. as is well known, we have put forward proposals for concrete action, particularly in relation to research in the field of security and defence and the development of a european defence equipment market. the proposals have been well received by the member states and i am pleased that the commission is now implementing some of them as of march this year. in this context, i would like to point out that an impact assessment study on the simplification of intra-community transfers of defence equipment is under way. as regards the issue of public procurement, a green paper is being prepared to launch the discussion on the appropriate set of rules for a cost-effective procurement of goods and services by the defence procurement agencies of the member states and the future european agency in a fully compatible and integrated manner. joint efforts with the european committee for standardisation (cen) on standardisation are continuing with a view to the development of a european handbook for defence contracts. the principles for economic control of the defence industry and market in the enlarged european union have been developed; and there has been progress on the control of exports of dual-use items in the wider context of the eu strategy and action plan against the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction. as regards research issues, i would like to inform you that the commission is finalising a communication on a preparatory action on the enhancement of the european industrial potential related to security research for the period 2004-2006. a call for proposals will be published early next year. a group of leading figures has been set up to advise and assist the commission in this task, which is expected to contribute to a substantial european safety research programme from 2007. the report by mr queiró broadly supports the commission's approach to strengthening the european defence industrial and technological base by gradually establishing a european defence equipment market and promoting security research. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. the report welcomes the implementation of pilot actions in the field of safety research and development. all these indications encourage the commission's action, and we are encouraged by the favourable opinion of the committee on industry, foreign trade, research and energy on the creation of the european common market for defence equipment and by the explicit support for various commission proposals in this respect. as regards the establishment of a defence agency, following the mandate of the thessaloniki european council, the member states in the council urged the commission to clarify how the community could work with and/or within the future agency in order to maximise synergies in pursuit of common objectives. the commission has responded favourably to this request and today here confirms its willingness and availability to contribute to this task by the means already presented in the communication of last march, which is the subject of this debate. in this spirit, the commission envisages involvement in the development and operation of the agency as a means of contributing to the achievement of its objectives as defined by the european council. in conclusion, i would like to stress the commission's appreciation and expectation of the european parliament's support for mr queiró's report and the close cooperation with the member states in order to move forward in an area full of challenges. the citizens and taxpayers of europe have a right to expect us to move towards greater effectiveness in the defence sector and a strengthened credibility of european security and defence policy.

- mr president, it is clear that if we want to develop credible cooperation in the field of defence in the future - i am not prejudging its form, its limits or its future legal status - the states concerned will have to support each other in the field of military equipment. however, the commission's communication of 11 march 2003 on this subject is disappointing for three main reasons. firstly, it deals with the question of the arms industries mainly from the point of view of the market and competition, because obviously this is where it has some competence. but this is a very narrow view, because in this area security concerns are and must remain predominant. the lower cost of acquiring equipment is an important consideration, certainly, especially in times of budget deficits, but it is by no means the only one. the states, in the name of their security, must remain the sole masters of their own judgments. this has always been recognized in article 296 of the treaty on the european community, which is renewed as it stands, i remind you, by article 342 of part three of the draft european constitution. secondly, the commission's communication tends to overcommunitarize, with codecision, including the creation of a community framework for defence equipment which would seem to include the armaments agency. such a communitarianisation is not at all in the interests of defence cooperation, which needs intergovernmental relations and variable geometries, under the control of national parliaments, so that member states are not discouraged from getting involved. i welcome the fact that this armaments agency, which is finally being set up on the basis of article 17 of the treaty on european union, is intergovernmental in nature. thirdly, i found in paragraph 6 of mr queiró's report - and i warmly welcome it - a key concept which is absent from the commission's communication, as indeed from the draft european constitution, namely the concept of community preference. i am not sure that the commissioner has been able to give us a clear answer to this question, but i am sure that he will be able to give us a clear answer to the question of the future of the european union. of course, this european preference must remain flexible, because high-tech military equipment is not agricultural products and, as i have already said, the states must remain in control of their security. however, even if a strict legal commitment cannot be made, there should at least be a declaration of intent somewhere. i thank mr queiró again for making this clear.

policy towards the region as it endeavours to support the countries in that region in their efforts to foster peace, democracy, respect for human rights and economic prosperity, and also to achieve stability in the region as a whole. the proposal being examined by parliament today, under which the stability pact would be included in the scope of council regulation (ec) no 1080/2000, will provide the pact with a sound and solid basis on which to fulfil the crucial mandate given by the international community. the stability pact is specifically designed to further foster regional cooperation, as was underlined by the thessaloniki agenda endorsed on 20 june 2003 by the european council. it will thereby complement the stabilisation and association process engaged with the western balkans. the commission therefore welcomes the positive opinion on the proposal and hopes that parliament will share the objective of having this new financial framework fully applicable as of 1 january 2004. the commission regards amendment 1 to article 1(2) as superfluous, since the principle of cost-sharing by member states is implicitly contained in article 2(2) of the regulation, and given that budget line 19 07 04 is an integral part of the budgetary discussion. with reference to amendment 2 to article 1a, as well as amendments 4 and 6, the commission can support the proposal that the appointment of the special coordinator of the stability pact be renewed on an annual basis. the commission also agrees with the wider objective of closely associating parliament in following the work of the stability pact. nevertheless, and bearing in mind the need to keep the appointment procedure as straightforward as possible, the commission cannot accept parliament's proposal, in amendment 2 to article 1a, to include formal consultation of the relevant european parliament committee. neither can it accept the insertion, in the form of a new article 1b proposed by amendments 3, 5 and 7, of a hearing before the committee. however, the commission agrees with amendments 4 and 6, with regard to ensuring that parliament is informed of the appointment proposal. the commission is happy, although it is not possible to include it in the new regulation, to make the commitment before parliament to arrange for an association with parliament in practice. in particular, the commission will, well in advance of the appointment decision, inform parliament, via the chairman of the committee on foreign affairs, human rights, common security and defence policy, of its appointment proposal. the appointed special coordinator will appear before the committee on foreign affairs as necessary, and at least twice at year, to report on its activities. the commission would be grateful if parliament could adopt a positive opinion during the present part-session, since it is eager to embark on the implementation stage immediately after the new regulation enters into force, in order to provide the special coordinator of the stability pact with the timely support that will allow him to fulfil his mandate in 2004. on behalf of the commission i wish to express special thanks to the rapporteur, mr swoboda, for the quality of his preparatory work and the very good relations he has maintained with the commission.

- the next item is the report (a5-0398/2003) by mr coelho, on behalf of the committee on civil liberties and human rights, on the proposal for a european parliament recommendation to the council on the second generation schengen information system (sis ii) [2003/2180 (ini) ].
- madam president, we have two reasons for rejecting this recommendation on the second generation schengen information system. we refuse to approve the electronic personal data filing system, which the author intends to perfect because it is a tool of police repression. and we reject even more the politics that this tool is intended to serve. the states for whom the fight against terrorism is a universal justification want this file to receive additional data and to be combined with the system that manages visas. consultation would be extended to judicial authorities that do not yet have access to it. this repressive tool is primarily designed to prevent migrant workers from coming to the european union, thereby threatening the freedom of all. spending millions of euros on sophisticated surveillance equipment and a system for sharing information on those who cross a border that was open to them and are now being slapped on the face is outrageous. this is how dramatic situations are created and perpetuated, on which unscrupulous smugglers thrive. we are opposed to the policy of a 'fortress europe' surrounded by barbed wire, whether electronic or simply legal. it is a backward, reactionary and inhumane policy. the fate of the peoples of the south of the european union has been linked since time immemorial to that of the peoples on the other side of the mediterranean, from morocco to egypt. the populations of the newly acceded countries of eastern europe are closely linked to the populations of the countries of the former soviet union. restricting freedom of movement between the european union and the surrounding countries sometimes means cutting people's flesh. we reject it and we will vote against it.
the commission. madam president, i have the greatest respect for critical views on the schengen information system. i will be honest, i do not think that the best strategy is to demonize the schengen information system, but everyone is responsible for his political positions. what i am saying to you clearly is that the schengen information system is essentially a system for managing the external border of the european union and that this is a fundamental condition for safeguarding freedom of movement within the european area. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the internal borders are not crossed. the fact is that this is not just a question of entering and leaving the territory of the european union, it is also a question of ensuring security within the territory of the european union. this is a different political choice from jaez, which i would like to reiterate here. i think the fundamental question is what the values of the schengen information system are. i have a christmas present for mr marco cappato, but it is not this one, because this would be a smaller one, it is another, we are waiting for natale. but, as to the question he asked, i would like to say two things: firstly, there is no provision for any form of transfer of schengen information system data to third countries. access to the schengen database is reserved for the member states of the european union. as regards the data to be integrated into the system, i think i gave the answer in my speech when i said that the debate on the specific data to be integrated into the system has not yet been concluded. we have made a feasibility study which we have sent to the european parliament, identifying the requests that have been made to us by the member states. the specific identification of these data is not yet complete and the commission is currently preparing a communication to be published by the end of this year, in which we will assess the state of the current debate. i understand the doubts and fears. there is one thing, however, that i would like to say: there is a big difference between the fact that i, as commissioner, am here to talk to you about the schengen ii information system and the fact that, in relation to the first system, there was no commissioner here to be responsible for what was being done. i am here today to say that the commission is going to present a proposal for harmonization on the control and protection of personal data in the third pillar and that there must be democratic control and judicial control of the operation of the system. this is what makes the schengen information system i different, and this difference was made possible precisely because the system was integrated into the whole of the community acquis with the support of this parliament, which i hope will continue to count on by voting in favour of mr carlos coelho's report.

- mr president, as you know, there are many opinion polls which show how far europe is from its citizens and how much more needs to be done to bring it closer to them. community action to promote european citizenship exists, but it is of course still insufficient. the decision to set up a grant programme to promote active european citizenship for a period of five years is a good thing. promoting the idea of european citizenship so that citizens can take ownership of europe and empower themselves to achieve this are of course the objectives of this proposal. the democratic legitimacy and transparency of the union should be strengthened. but to do this we must also simplify all the procedures that will enable as many associations as possible to benefit from this tool. in addition, we see a hierarchy between the organisations which, i regret, is not always justified. objective criteria should be defined by the european commission to finance the operation and activities of the various ngos, especially those that intervene directly on the ground to bring our values of solidarity to life. let us not forget that it is thanks to them that social cohesion is maintained in our european suburbs, where exclusion and discrimination are rampant. how can we make young people believe that europe is a reality and give them confidence if this europe does not fight discrimination in practice? in practice, it is said that the commission has special relations with certain associations. if that claim were true, this situation would not be acceptable. moreover, if the emphasis is on the social dimension, and we thank the rapporteur for that, we cannot spare the political dimension, which is essential to reduce the current democratic deficit. so, what kind of citizenship are we talking about? the report states that citizenship of the union complements and extends national citizenship by recognising common rights. it is the result of the need felt by the members of this community to share common democratic values in the process of building the union. can we continue to talk about a european construction which excludes 15 to 18 million residents of europe who are not community nationals? by their active participation in the construction of europe, they are citizens of europe on an equal footing with others, and their associations and ngos are also active structures that help to promote europe. it is clear that we want a europe of citizens, a europe which is truly democratic and based on solidarity, and to achieve this we must innovate and improve european citizenship. in the era of free movement of capital, goods and people, it goes without saying that people must be able to assume their responsibilities and enjoy their rights, regardless of the country in which they have chosen to reside within the european area. europe cannot accept a hierarchy of citizens which would give some a higher degree of equality than others. all those who share the same european space must be able to enjoy equal rights in the country where they live every day. to do this, we must base european citizenship on residence and no longer on citizenship. all too often in europe nationality and citizenship are inseparable. in this respect, the acceding countries can provide us with an interesting experience, since for them the concept of citizenship is different from that of nationality. we want our old europe to be inspired by this new breath to give europe a new citizenship based on residence.
- (pt) mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, we have begun to feel the consolidation of european citizenship through a series of events such as the introduction of the euro or the abolition of the internal frontiers of the community. in such situations, it is clear that the existence of this european citizenship is complementary to national citizenship. however, there are areas where consolidation is less visible. the structures created by the community to promote this european citizenship receive community funds and may even have achieved something, but they do not reach the majority of citizens. the lack of recognition of the work done by the various institutions is profound. however, the lack of transparency, the bureaucracy and the obvious gap between european recently to find that european citizens are completely unaware of the work of the convention, despite the considerable resources invested in informing them. two years ago, i myself wrote a report on the euro, a major community service essential to mobility and the promotion of crossborder work, and i realised that citizens were generally unaware of this. two years on and although this area was strategically identified in the resolution we voted on, which stressed the need for a major awareness-raising campaign, the situation remains essentially unchanged, due to the failings of the organisations receiving these funds. this is a way of gradually erasing the image of a europe of eurocrats only and far from the citizens, by letting them know that europe acts directly and on a daily basis for each of us and also by offering the opportunity for citizens to participate genuinely in social and political matters. the community institutions are not entirely blameless and can improve european union. the intergovernmental conference is preparing a new treaty with constitutional aspirations which will have a significant impact on the future of european citizens. i therefore issue a to do. consultation is required in all the member states on the future treaty. in this way we can all contribute to the real exercise of active european citizenship. it is foolish to tell our fellow citizens that we are also european citizens and then spend our time telling them to shut up. it is not right, having proclaimed european citizenship in maastricht, to then ensure that nothing is said about it by imposing a strict vow of silence on citizens. we cannot accept the idea that european citizenship is all right as long as citizens do not commit the sin of asking for the floor. let us therefore commit ourselves to active european citizenship.

in writing. - (pt) we welcome the rejection of the directive on port services. this result is the culmination of an intense struggle by the trade unions in the sector - which have had our support and that of our political group - as evidenced by the large demonstrations in front of the european parliament in march 2003 and in barcelona and rotterdam last september, as well as a petition filed this week and accompanied by more than 16 000 signatures of workers, not to mention strikes, demonstrations and other actions. the entire trade union movement in the sector opposed this directive and the agreement, now rejected, reached at a conciliation meeting between the council and the european parliament. this directive was an additional element of the overall package included in the 'lisbon strategy', which aims to accelerate the process of liberalisation and market opening in various sectors, from postal services to port services. this is not only a violent attack on the public service, but it is also a challenge to the very concept of public service. the agreement rejected today would have promoted, through the principle of self-help, social dumping and the gradual erosion of dockers' wage and working conditions. it did not recognise the public nature of port services and left them to the law of the market and the primacy of competition. it did not even retain the system of prior authorisation for service providers.

in writing. - (pt) i welcome the results of the conciliation procedure and have expressed my vote in writing. throughout this complex process, the text has evolved considerably, from a very negative text in decisive aspects to a text providing balanced solutions, leading to clearer and more transparent rules in access to the market for port services - for those who wish to do so, of course. the use of the controversial 'self-help' system would have been limited to the ship's crew alone, in association with the competent port operator. in the case of piloting, member states were left with sufficient leeway to subject the compulsory authorisation to strict standards and qualifications. finally, the broad general framework of the principle of subsidiarity would have been respected. each port or port facility would have been obliged to provide information on its own financial relations, thus avoiding distortions of competition. i therefore consider that this result was positive - i am speaking of course of the result that could have been obtained in view of the composition of the interests involved and the controversy raised by this question. i regret that a small majority rejected the conciliation. i fear that we will return to the worst of the stages of this procedure and thereby delay port development for many years to come. i am also surprised that at the time of the final vote more than a dozen voting machines had mysteriously broken down, all the members having voted in favour, and that, despite the immediate demands, the president had not resumed the vote.

mr president, commissioner, president of the council, ladies and gentlemen! we have already debated the stability and growth pact in strasbourg on 21 october 2002. i made it clear at the time that there is no objection to limiting the new debt of public budgets, if this is coupled with the need to generate growth and stimulate demand. but growth and demand growth are not to be achieved by lowering wages or extending working hours, but by tax relief for lower and middle income groups, public investment, expansionary investment by companies and increased private consumption. the outcome of the euro finance ministers' meeting, freezing the deficit procedure against germany and france and giving these countries a delay until 2005 to reach the 3% annual debt ceiling, is a rotten compromise. this compromise does not change the basic false construction that in difficult economic times strict adherence to the 3% limit has a procyclical rather than an anticyclical effect. reform of the stability pact must be accompanied by a reinforced european economic, social, employment, tax and environmental policy in order to stimulate investment in general. it must be possible to make public investment financed by credit, even if this temporarily raises the deficit ratio above 3%. i think this is an honest and correct step, because otherwise we lose all credibility and every year more and more countries are faced with the same problem. my opinion - yours may be different - is that you should correct mistakes and not try to hide them by making new ones.

(es) madam president, first of all, since there have been no specific questions but several speeches which have touched on the subject, i would like to make a clarification on eurostat. as we have already informed the cocobu on several occasions, the court has not carried out any complete audit of the statistical office, of eurostat. however, the court has examined some programmes implemented by eurostat in the context of other audits. the results of these audits were included in our annual reports for 1993, 1998 and 1999, the latter published in november 2000. our comments on the management of eurostat concern the inadequate procedures for awarding certain contracts and the misuse of the technical assistance offices, the so-called bat. it should be noted that the court had already made observations on bat as a result of other audits. in 1999 the commission reviewed the procedures for awarding contracts and the use of bat in response to these observations. the commission introduced new management and control rules in these two areas. in mid-2000 olaf also launched an internal investigation into eurostat. in view of these elements, new rules and olaf's investigation, it would not have been appropriate to launch an audit on eurostat at that time. i would like to stress that the court generally refrains from carrying out audits in the departments and areas where olaf carries out its investigations. we want to avoid any interference or action which could harm the anti-fraud investigation. the court will take into account eurostat's lessons when carrying out its risk analysis for the coming year. on the other hand, mr kuhne has made a comment which i appreciate, but i do not think there was any question addressed to the court of auditors. mr mulder says we're on the right track, but not for long. i think if we're going to be on the right track, we have to keep it. how long? it all depends on the organization, on the institution, on whether it is more or less complicated, or more or less extensive. the commission, given its size and geographical spread - it is certainly not alone and each of the changes it makes has a national impact and therefore has to be in constant contact with the different member states and cannot always maintain the cruising speed that can be set at a given moment - is not making reforms for the next five years either, but we believe that it is something that goes much further. i think we are on the right track, and that is also why parliament is here, to keep the commission awake and to keep this reform going. the truth is that since 1994 there has been a positive sdr despite a number of shortcomings in the accounting system. for this reason, in december 2002 the commission decided to carry out an accounting reform with the aim of making it operational in 2005. i still think that the date is optimistic, and i am not saying this to argue with the commission, but to ensure that you do not become discouraged if the year 2005 comes and the reform is not 100 per cent complete. we in the court of auditors believe that the time is short. we believe that it is better to take each step safely, rather than in haste, so that the decisions taken will stand and that reforms will not be an eternal "penelopism" of doing and undoing. on the other hand, since we are talking about reform, i also think it is important that this blow which all of us europeans have received with the eurostat case, when we thought that the bats and certain situations had been completed, should not undermine the reform. what this situation makes very clear is the urgency of continuing the reform and completing it as soon as possible. here's the situation. the problem is encrypting the improvement. you know the court has never been a friend of error rate talk. why would you do that? in writing. - last night at the end of the debate we were astonished to see the commission throwing off its mask and declaring that it would not propose in any case the extension of the experimental reduction of vat rates for labour-intensive services, even if the member states unanimously requested it (as was the case on 25 november). we thus see both the undemocratic nature of the monopoly of initiative and the arrogance of the commission when it uses it to defend its power interests. because it's all about power. the commission wants to move towards a 'country of origin' vat system which will give it a central role and more power. this is why it proposed its so-called 'rationalization' plan, in which the perpetuation of certain reduced rates was only a decoy. the professions, particularly those in the catering and construction industries, are thus held hostage by the commission. we hope that the ministers will put their hands on the table and take this into account in the work of the intergovernmental conference. in the meantime, we support the excellent randzio-plath report, which has clearly understood the issues.
in writing. - i agree with our rapporteur that i do not think it is appropriate to harmonise vat rates without first improving the economic and fiscal system of the member states as a whole. in the difficult economic and social times we are living in, the economic system advocated by the commission and the intangible respect for the maastricht criteria demonstrate the need for a minimum of flexibility. each state must have at its disposal all its cyclical, economic and monetary instruments to act in the most appropriate way. direct and indirect taxation are among the instruments which the eu must be able to use as it sees fit, because each economy is unique, even if it is an integral part of a globalised system. the problems are not necessarily the same in different countries, so the solutions must be different. it is all these reasons which have led me, and the colleagues in my delegation, to call on behalf of france for the continuation of the reduced vat rates in annex h, in particular for catering, accommodation and recording services.
in writing. - four years of reduced vat rates do not allow us to see the full effects of this experiment, especially since some employers, knowing that it was temporary, did not implement it. however, all the professionals consulted affirm that the reduction in vat has positive economic impacts which are not negligible. the number of employees in the housekeeping sector in france has increased by 8.6% in two years. that is why we must continue along this path. as rapporteur for an opinion, i can only welcome the commission's text and in particular annex h, extending annex k to certain services, such as catering. since each member state is free to choose to apply a reduced rate in a category listed in annex h, not all sectors which have benefited from the experience should now be excluded from the scope of the directive. that is why i voted in favour of the amendments of the committee on economic and monetary affairs. amendments nos 22 and 23, which i tabled with astrid lulling for the plenary session, are also very important. they allow the experiment to be extended until the entry into force of this amendment to the directive, which is absolutely necessary in order to avoid disastrous consequences for employment.
in writing. - three priority sectors must be able to benefit on a lasting basis from the reduced rate of vat in france: the building sector, the catering sector and the record industry. since it has no impact on competition, this decision should be the exclusive responsibility of the states, deciding according to their own priorities. for france, these priorities are: job creation, the reduction of undeclared work and cultural development. but the european commission does not agree with this: instead of giving up its unsuccessful attempts to harmonize vat and allow the states to regain their freedom, it wants to increase its powers by imposing the rapid extinction of derogations. commissioner bolkestein cynically said last night that although the council had unanimously demanded that the reduced rate for labour-intensive services be maintained, the commission had no intention of making a proposal to that effect and would instead initiate proceedings, as from 1 july 2004, against states which maintained these reduced rates. this blockade by the commission, which is holding our professions hostage in order to increase its own powers, is unacceptable and shows that any transfer of competence must remain reversible.

in writing. - the report deals with the procedure for adopting derogating measures concerning the development of a common system of value added tax. if the european institutions were concerned with the interests of the majority of the population, they would standardize vat by proposing... its abolition, which would at the same time simplify the procedure... but of course the european institutions, like the national states, are mainly keen to relieve the burden of taxation from private enterprises and the privileged social classes by making the population, including the poorest, bear the bulk of the burden. indirect taxes, including vat, are used for this purpose. they are particularly unfair because, not being proportional to income, they hit the poor harder than the rich. we have of course voted against the report.
in writing. - (pt) the apparent objective of this proposal for a directive is to avoid double taxation of corporate profits, to be precise to ensure that profits taxed and paid as dividends by a subsidiary company to its parent company are not taxed twice. in reality, the directive seeks to remove the tax 'disadvantage' between multinational and national groups, thus responding to the demands of the 'business world'. the basis of the proposal is therefore to extend the scope of the directive to more types of commercial companies and to lower the minimum threshold for holding a shareholding from 25% to 10% in order to have one company recognised as a parent company and the other as a subsidiary, with the aim of guaranteeing exemptions, for example, from withholding tax. the rapporteur, who would have preferred that there was no minimum threshold, proposes a threshold of 5%, which is lower than the commission's proposal. in other words, the relevant issue is not so much double taxation but finding the legal means for multinational groups to manage their tax benefits by allowing them to use cross-border exemptions and deductions to de facto reduce the tax on their profits and thus increase the 'legal' possibilities for tax evasion, which is unacceptable. portugal is one of the three countries where this threshold is around 25%, and this directive will therefore increase the pressure for a change in the regime applicable to national groups.
in writing. - some meps would like the staff representatives of the companies concerned to be better informed in the event of takeover bids than is provided for in this directive. i guess so. but why does one of these amendments propose at the same time the acceptance of 'confidentiality clauses', which means ultimately reserving information to a few delegates and forbidding it to all workers? and even if these amendments were adopted, they would not in the least protect workers from the dramatic consequences of stock market takeovers, especially collective redundancies under the pretext of restructuring. the european authorities are concerned with unifying the jungle of this system, as here in the case of takeover bids. but they are laughing at those who, year after year, takeover bid or not, find themselves more and more in the streets because reducing the workforce and, therefore, the wage bill, is one of the ways for capital holders to raise the price of their shares on the stock market. only a ban on collective redundancies could protect workers from the dramatic consequences of takeovers on their jobs. we voted against this report.
in writing. - (de) for more than a decade we have been debating the takeover bid directive. the first version failed to overcome the last obstacle here in the house. i am glad to see that, thanks to the negotiations involving the council and our rapporteur mr lehne, the adoption of this important text is finally close. the italian-portuguese compromise reached in the council and adopted by the committee on legal affairs and internal market and the committee on economic and monetary affairs appears to be the best possible outcome in a complex situation. to stipulate that articles 9 and 11 are applicable throughout europe while allowing member states not to make them binding on their businesses is not ideal, but it is the only possible compromise. the alternative would be to have no directive and nobody wants that. a small step in the right direction is always better than years of idleness. i think there are a few strategic areas where special rights should be granted to member states for use in public procurement. the report under consideration indirectly covers the possibility for member states to rely on such rights and also solves the specifically scandinavian problem of values with multiple voting rights, without jeopardising the importance of a level playing field, which guarantees equal opportunities for businesses. in writing. - in the present european context, particularly in view of the problems raised by taxation, particularly indirect taxation, i cannot accept the commission's proposal to abolish the vat exemption for postal services. given that the sixth directive of 1977 has not yet been updated, that problems of approximation of vat rates persist, and that the postal sector undergoing liberalization has not yet been the subject of an impact study, how can such a proposal be made? apart from vat, how can we believe in healthy competition for the benefit of users in the member states when the commission proposes an optional reduced rate for conventional postal services, which can only highlight the technical problems linked to weight and the disparities in rates between member states. once again the commission is putting the cart before the horse by trying to convince us by the coué method: well, we are not fooled and reject this text.
in writing. - (pt) the commission's proposal aims to abolish the vat exemption for postal services, which has existed since the sixth vat directive of 1977. the commission thus pursues two objectives: to continue the process of introducing a single vat system and to contribute to the ongoing liberalisation of postal services at eu level, as recommended by directive 2002/39/ec. thus, following this process of gradual liberalisation - which i reject because it undermines the public service and its universal character - the abolition of the obligation for public operators to charge the full rate of vat would have the effect of increasing the cost of the services provided, especially for private individuals, and of encouraging the outsourcing of services. i therefore agree with the economic and monetary affairs committee of the european parliament in recommending that this commission proposal be rejected, although this is not the position of the rapporteur. i therefore welcome the rejection of the amendments tabled by the rapporteur himself, with the support of his group and the epp-ed, which sought a compromise that would allow the adoption of this proposal for a directive.
- mr president, madam commissioner, first of all i would like to congratulate our rapporteurs, jan mulder and neena gill, as well as the whole committee on budgets and its staff, for the preparation of this 2004 budget. it was conducted in an unusually serene manner, with a new budgetary framework and in the context of enlarged europe. i think that our committee has reached a maturity in compromise for this parliament and has been able to work out a working method under the leadership of our chairman, mr wynn, a working method which is bearing fruit particularly this year. the priorities of our group have been heard, retained and strengthened. i am thinking of community policies in favour of enterprises, and particularly small and mediumsized enterprises, and of all those policies which contribute to the construction of a people's europe, such as the twinning arrangements in the enlarged europe, and which give visibility to europe's action in the world, such as the appropriations for vaccination against poverty-related diseases. a budget that is calm, but one that is surrounded by a general challenge to parliament's powers in budgetary matters. we have had to endure the provocations of the council to the end with regard to our rights and prerogatives. with what result? it is high time to reflect on the worrying gap between political rhetoric and budgetary executability. every year i denounce this problem, which has become recurrent. the council's frivolous attitude is contrary to our legitimate budgetary ambitions. the brussels fiasco has shown what our heads of state and government have in store for europe. a real involvement of europe in the lives of its citizens cannot be achieved without far-reaching policies. and large-scale policies require a large budget. the council seems not to have heard this, focusing on the stability pact and the sum of national selfishness. is this the europe we want to build? i certainly don't. it is the one we are being pushed towards. we had an example of this inconsistency with information policy when the budget was voted. we want to bring europe closer to the citizens, we are worried about the general public's disengagement from the construction of europe and we are trying to federate peoples around major projects. all this requires a coherent and ambitious information and communication policy. however, without parliament's intervention, the appropriations allocated to this policy would have suffered from the council's budget cuts. but the most serious problem is the weakening of our budget, with payment appropriations falling this year to less than 0.99% of gdp, the lowest level since 1987. i therefore agree with the remarks of president cox and the analysis of mr prodi in his reply to the six heads of state who call for a reduction in the ceiling on payment appropriations to 1% of gnp. where is the coherence with the lisbon project, the growth project, the competitiveness project for the union? there are no miracles. the squaring of the circle has never been proved. being head of state or government means being responsible. it is therefore about ensuring that the means and objectives are appropriate. if the council wants to lead us into a deadlock, it is up to us, the european parliament, to remind it of its promises. and i do not see how we can finance these crucial reforms with ever-diminishing means. the european parliamentarians elected by the people are responsible elected representatives. thank you, mrs. schreyer, for calling him back. they know how to draw up the union's budgets in accordance with budgetary orthodoxy. but they also know that the union's budget must respect the political priorities decided upon, co-decided upon. the council must respect parliament today and must have more confidence in our assembly, which enjoys the legitimacy of the ballot box, in the future.
- i think, mr mulder, that the applause from all the benches in this house shows you how grateful this house is for your work. the debate is closed. the vote on this important matter will take place on thursday at 11.30 a.m.
- the 2004 budget of the enlarged europe is less than 1% of gross national income. since 1997, it has never been lower. commitments are decreasing; the payments are decreasing. the structural funds and agricultural expenditure are also falling. the appropriations for external aid under heading 4 are now reduced to the appropriate amount: eur 35 million is thus taken from aid to latin america. financial pressures on fundamental elements of community policy, such as human rights or the duty to assist the weakest, are accompanied by a devastating squeeze on development aid funds. in these circumstances, how can we expect poverty to be eradicated by 2015? the question of the funds for iraq is not primarily financial. the urgent thing is to end the occupation. the iraqi people must regain their sovereignty as soon as possible so that they can assess their own needs and organise the means to meet them. the use of the flexibility instrument would raise €95 million. the solution proposed - to reduce appropriations under heading 4 still further - is not acceptable. this budget does not meet the challenges that the eu should face today for a fairer and more united world.
