the rapporteur. - mr president, commissioner, we are discussing this evening the legislative package relating to the revision of the legislation on human and veterinary medicines. this revision represents two years of work, more than two years of joint work, research, questions, negotiations, two years which i hope will be concluded tomorrow with a successful vote. i would like to thank very sincerely my colleagues in the european parliament, all the groups, with whom i have had many meetings, and in particular my colleague mrs müller. i thank her for her efficient cooperation. i listened to the requests of my colleagues. i defended their arguments to the council. i have included them in all my steps so that today's result is shared by all. i would also like to thank the european commission, in particular commissioner liikanen, whose brilliant team i have seen to be very dedicated and have appreciated the quality of our exchanges. i would also like to thank the council for the constructive approach it has taken to these issues in order to reach agreement at second reading. but all this thanks will be in vain if tomorrow each member of this house does not show responsibility by not adopting the negotiated compromise and voting in favour of other amendments which, i believe, reflect more individual interests than collective interests. yes, we have a compromise, and a compromise does not satisfy everything. but what progress, what progress we have made in public and animal health! the goal of balance, so difficult to achieve at the outset, has been achieved. we wanted to bring the different partners together, in particular to bring health care and innovation face to face. however, the analysis showed that generic drugs and innovations by pharmaceutical companies are not contradictory. these are not two opposing products but complementary ones. generics do not develop without innovation and innovation is still encouraged by the availability of generic medicines. protecting the health of the patient means being able to combat the development of new diseases, to deal with old plagues that reappear or to cure more effectively. protecting the health of the patient means giving scientific research the effective means to discover either new molecules or an innovative therapeutic use for an existing medicine. innovation comes at a cost. we must not forget that protecting our health requires considerable financial investment. data protection is therefore essential to guarantee medical progress, our european medical progress of which we are proud. the result of our compromise is 8 + 2 + 1 and that is what we shall vote on tomorrow in the sitting. development and research form the basis of health protection, which would not be complete without the availability of generic medicines. generics are very important for our european health systems and for patients. i therefore welcome the direction taken by these directives. the terminology 'generic medicinal products' is introduced for the first time. it is also proposed that the bolar system be introduced in the union, which we have improved by our amendments. this will speed up the availability of all generics. my colleagues in the house and the council have also accepted my proposal, called the 'eurogeneric' which will avoid any blocking of the development of these products, particularly in the candidate countries. the review of pharmaceutical legislation is not only about finding the optimum balance between generics and innovations. many other equally important aspects were considered. i am thinking in particular of the definitions of medicinal product, generic medicinal product and biosimilar medicinal product. there have been tense debates on these issues. personally, i have always advocated a product safety approach. having too broad definitions would be counterproductive for manufacturers and patients. we have reached a satisfactory balance on this point, as we have on frontier products. i know that this is still a matter of some debate. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial interests are protected. making a list of exemptions also did not seem to be the right solution. such a list would never have been exhaustive. the existing legislation on cosmetics, food supplements, medical devices, to name just a few, is in place. they are legally valid, it is not a question of challenging them but of solving a very real problem. i have a request to make to the commission on this point and i would like the commission to make a commitment in this respect in order to increase legal certainty for operators: it would certainly be appropriate for your competent departments to bring together as soon as possible all the parties concerned, whom i have mentioned above. i think that would be particularly important to put people's minds at ease. thus, on the basis of these exchanges and in the light of the judgments already given by the court of justice of the european communities, a concerted and formal commitment on interpretation could emerge. i really hope that this proposal will be followed up, and i also expect the commission to make clear its commitment to the doha declaration. i know that this is also an essential point for many of my colleagues in the house. the authorisation of a medicinal product for human or veterinary use does not mean that the control of its efficacy and safety has come to an end. as such, strengthening pharmacovigilance has been one of our priorities. this has made it necessary to make changes to the existing arrangements. first, by creating the possibility of carrying out unannounced checks at the source of manufacture. secondly, by shortening the deadlines for the mandatory submission of periodic reports, also by setting up a system for the rapid exchange of data collected by all partners, by ensuring consistency of pharmacovigilance systems between member states. we also stressed the independence of pharmacovigilance and asked that the management of funds for these activities remain under the permanent control of the competent authorities. my colleagues and i also wanted to take the environmental aspect of the drug into account. this point was raised with the executive director of the medicines agency in london, who confirmed the validity of our approach. however, in no case should a marketing authorisation be refused on the basis of this criterion. we all know, for example, that chemotherapy products can cause harmful environmental releases, but we cannot imagine banning their authorization. that would be nonsense. the aim is to better assess this environmental risk and, for all classes of therapeutics, to take effective measures to reduce impacts. this is a very important point for our parliament. i also wanted to return to the question of information, and my colleagues supported me in this. it is our responsibility to deal with the problems that arise. it would have been easy to dismiss the subject, but that was not our position. we therefore ask the european commission to present a clear text on what is available in this area, to analyse the potential benefits and risks of this dissemination of information to patients, to consider the responsibility of the issuer and to submit proposals to us. however, i have some regrets about these reports. the most important concerns the scope of the directive and the council's refusal to introduce immediately the mandatory centralised procedure for all new active substances. on this point, parliament has been too european for the council. however, in the compromise, important pathologies were included in this scope and a revision clause in four years will strengthen this system and increase equal access to health for every european citizen. i congratulate my colleague, mrs müller, who negotiated this. the committee on the environment, public health and consumer protection has tabled a number of amendments to the proposal. it would seem to me inconsistent and even very dangerous that the professionals who will be appointed should have a similar level of expertise. it is the criterion of expertise, not nationality, that will guarantee the quality and effectiveness of scientific evaluation. we will be very vigilant on this point. the house also adopted a resolution on the situation in the former yugoslavia. i am well aware of this, but progress has been made in the area of mutual recognition. this provision will ensure the development of this class of medicines. we must look at what is proposed and not just stick to what has not been agreed in the negotiations. this is an important perspective and shows that homeopathic medicines have not been neglected, nor have veterinary medicines been sacrificed. all the provisions i have mentioned above apply to all veterinary medicinal products. these directives are not, as i have heard, intended to impede social security systems, to favour one sector over another. on the contrary, they ensure the development of a high level of health protection. they promote access to products for all patients, and they encourage scientific research by addressing the vital growth of generic medicine. nor do they divide the current 15 member states or the enlargement countries. i hope that tomorrow, when we vote, we will be able to achieve this success for our three institutions in the field of human and animal health. i am confident that there is an agreement, a commitment by the majority of the political groups, and i dare not imagine that it will not be respected.
- mr president, we have been working successfully for two years on this matter of the revision of european legislation on medicines. so it is true that i had hoped for much more than this compromise package negotiated with the council and the commission which will be put to the vote tomorrow. in my view, this procedure for reviewing the procedures for authorising the placing on the european market of human and veterinary medicinal products should lead to a radical change in the criteria for evaluating and authorising medicinal products in the interests of patients, public health and healthcare professionals. the first aim of this review was to have all new substances recognised by the european agency. in reality, the centralised procedure will only cover a few diseases. the london agency has widened its scope of action sufficiently to secure its funding, but the national authorities have retained the most lucrative classes of medicines, namely those for neurodegenerative or cardiovascular diseases. the interests of the commission and the council are safe, but are they those of the patients? in the interests of patients, we have advanced pharmacovigilance and transparency in addition to braille, but it is true that some last-minute compromises by the council have subtly weakened these achievements. most drug evaluation documents should be publicly available, but what about pharmacovigilance reports? the public authorities responsible for issuing licences should be independent of firms but in fact remain under the yoke of private royalties. patients do not have the means to report drug side effects directly to the competent authorities and doctors are not obliged to do so. but a great victory: advertising for prescription drugs has been rejected, but for how long? in terms of public health, the environmental impact of new medicines should be assessed. this should not be the only evaluation criterion, but it should be taken into account in the benefit-risk balance of a medicinal product and therefore be part of the conditions for granting marketing authorisation. the environmental risk goes far beyond damage to nature, pollution linked to the release of toxic drug residues is a danger to human health. of course, therapies whose medical benefit outweighs the environmental risks must continue to be used. however, where effective alternatives exist, they should be promoted. unfortunately, the final wording of the amendments does not fully recognise the scale of the problem. as a doctor, i find that the evaluation of the effectiveness of medicines in comparison with others is sorely lacking in the new pharmaceutical package. the safety and quality of new substances is the only thing that matters. it does not matter whether they provide a significant clinical benefit or not. i tried to get the concept of therapeutic value added to be accepted in order to encourage firms to research truly innovative substances, but i met with opposition from all the institutions. i am sure, however, that this debate will come back to this house, because the pharmaceutical industry no longer wants to just put fake new treatments on the market and overprotect them for years. it is true that the major point of friction has been the authorisation of generic medicines. the pharmaceutical industry is trying to delay the sale of generic products, and that's normal. but this reaction was echoed by the commission and some colleagues, who restricted their definition, tightened the conditions for granting and extended the time limits by various tricks: switches, new indications, etc. despite the opposition of a majority of member states faced with the problem of financing their social security, european medicines will have the longest period of administrative data protection in the world. i also wonder whether these protections are compatible with the doha provisions requiring the manufacture of generics for export. this is certainly the major concern of this legislation for the financing of public health. finally, homeopathic medicines are another major disappointment. in fact, and in conclusion, i am pleased to admit that we have made considerable progress, but it is true that much remains to be done in the coming years.

doyle, but it is not absolutely certain that it would produce the results we have achieved today. so tomorrow, please vote on the compromises and, above all, do not take the risk and responsibility of failing to achieve what we have achieved after weeks of work.

- mr president, i would like to remind you once again, on behalf of my colleagues in the mpf delegation to the european parliament, that we are absolutely opposed to the payment of the main allowance of members of the european parliament from the community budget. under the treaty, meps are the representatives of their respective peoples and must therefore be paid by them. similarly, the currently lame compromise on taxation is not acceptable. the principle is simple and clear: members of the european parliament must be subject to the same taxes as their fellow citizens. if, unfortunately, the status under discussion today were to result - as one might fear - in increased parliamentary allowances and reduced income taxes, if, in addition, it gave the impression that meps were escaping the financial controls of their own country and becoming employees of the brussels entity, then, i tell you plainly, our fellow citizens would not accept that and that would be another terrible blow to the union's credibility. the governments must therefore resist the pressure of the federalists who want to detach the members of the european parliament from their respective countries, on the pretext of a principle of equality between members which does not exist anywhere in the treaties, and which is totally invented. we must strengthen the link between the member and his nation, to bring europe closer to the citizens. in summary, mr president, the main parliamentary allowance must be paid by the member's country of origin. income tax must be national. the compensation for costs must cover the actual costs. finally, as a compromise, it could be accepted that the daily allowance be regarded as supplementary income paid by the european institutions and subject to community taxation as such. this is the maximum acceptable for us.
- mr president, the situation in côte d'ivoire is deteriorating. we condemned the concept of "ivory", which tarnished the electoral legitimacy of laurent gbagbo, but we also condemned the military mutiny, which is unacceptable in a democracy. we were sceptical about the signing of the marcoussis peace agreement, which bore the marks of the dictate of the former colonial power. as expected, it was not viable and resulted in the resignation in september of rebel ministers from the government of national reconciliation. while some progress has been made in recent months, the resumption of fighting over the past fortnight has weakened the chances of reviving the peace process. today, the violence in the north, as in the "cocoa loop", the excesses of the so-called patriotic forces lead to the multiplication of violations of human rights. we ask that they stop as soon as possible and that the government and the rebel forces stop exploiting these demonstrations which are, in reality, nothing spontaneous. we demand that investigative procedures be put in place to punish those responsible for the abuses. we also strongly condemn the murder of the french journalist jean hélène and call for an international investigation to bring those responsible to justice. we call for the resumption of genuine negotiations to bring an end to the conflict. only by taking account of all the political forces in the country and the balance between them can a peaceful and democratic solution be found for the relaunch of the peace process, which can only be achieved through the disarmament of the militias and free general elections under international control. to do this, the structural causes - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i would like to thank you for your report. there are times when heads of state just go crazy! i think one of the tricks is to simply say: we want to lift the arms embargo on china. the arms embargo is a political pressure device, which means that there must be a political answer to the question of what has changed in china. tibet is still under chinese military occupation. taiwan is still threatened by china. human rights are still not respected in china. democracy is not in sight in china. you can do business with china. keep doing business with china! selling nuclear plants to china is foolish and harmful. but that is another matter, we must discuss it with the german chancellor. what i mean is that it would not only be wrong to say that you want to lift the arms embargo, but it would also be wrong to even say that there is any discussion at all at the moment about doing so. it simply means that we say to the chinese, "it's wonderful how you do this. keep arresting people for speaking their minds. we're not bothered by it at all. we're ready to do all kinds of business with you! secondly, there is another point: mr chirac and mr schröder - and these are really two heads of government whom i support in certain political situations, as in the case of the war in iraq. i have a terrible idea: did they buy china's partnership with such a strategy? in writing. - for the reasons of principle which i mentioned in my speech during the debate, i voted against the resolution of our assembly which again calls for a unified statute for members of the european parliament. i would add that the further we go in negotiating this status, the more difficulties we encounter, the more complexities we invent to solve these difficulties, and the more unsustainable the proposed system becomes. in particular, it is difficult to imagine how, in the name of a principle of equality between meps which does not exist, deep and very real inequalities could be created at the level of each country. how could the mep from a new member country, for example, be paid at a level twenty times that of a national mep? and how can such inequality be corrected? similar questions arise in the field of taxation: how can we imagine that a relatively well-paid mep pays income tax at a rate much lower than that of his fellow citizens? as i said in the debate, the dogmatic obstinacy of certain federalist members is creating a tangle which will be very damaging, once again, to the image of the european union.
in writing. - legislation on environmental liability is like opening pandora's box, since environmental damage is ill-defined and its scope of application is vague, particularly in the area of biodiversity, which is already governed by two major international conventions, those of berne and bonn. the repair should be limited to natura 2000 areas only and exclude non-profit-making activities such as leisure from professional activities. however, the directive does not distinguish between these two types of activity. for liability to apply, it must be based on objective and quantifiable criteria: the nature of the damage and its impact, the state of the environment at the time of the damage and, above all, local circumstances. the polluter pays principle must be effectively applied and not replaced by the taxpayer pays principle. the responsibility must include gmos and hydrocarbons, sensitive subjects, which are excluded from its scope. more generally, what is the point of recognising the european commission as having jurisdiction, when the criminalisation of environmental crime is a matter for judicial cooperation and other legal instruments such as the council of europe's lugano convention could be used?
in writing. - the grossetête report on the establishment of a community code relating to medicinal products for human use is intended, in essence, to protect the interests of the pharmaceutical industry. it is appalling that the profit-seeking interests of the big pharmaceutical companies should prevail in a field where public health should be the priority. the protection of the patent monopoly, which ensures the profits of this industry by driving up the prices of medicines, has the dramatic consequence of preventing hundreds of thousands of people from accessing medicines. we supported amendments to inform the public about the effects of medicines or to improve labelling, but we voted against amendments to protect the monopoly of pharmaceutical laboratories. in our view, public health and the interests of patients come before free trade and shareholder profit.
in writing. - we have just voted on the revision of the pharmaceutical legislation. the amended directive will make it possible to increase the degree of harmonisation of the rules governing medicinal products between the member states. it can increase the efficiency of the operation of centralised and decentralised procedures. but we want the member states to ensure that homeopathic medicines manufactured and marketed in the community are favoured. we voted for amendments which could solve some of the problems caused by the legal vacuum in which certain homeopathic medicines still exist. these medicines, used by more than 100 million europeans, not only do not cause side effects, but they also save money for health systems. we are absolutely keen to preserve homeopathic medicines which meet the demands of the citizens of our countries. we also spoke in favour of developing the european generic pharmaceutical industry, because if we want to preserve our social protection, we have to save money and generic medicines are part of that effort.
in writing. - the resolution on the commission's work programme for 2004 contains very strong passages, which i fully supported, on the eurostat case and its aftermath. no one can explain the commission's lack of reaction for such a long time. the commission has also been asked to provide a report on the implementation of the new financial regulation, which will be published in the official journal of the european union. these imperatives are all the more urgent as other abuses are constantly being discovered, for example the offences initiated on the fixing of prices in the agricultural management committees, or more recently the 'blue dragon 2000' case concerning the use of community funds in catalonia. these deviations are not unrelated to the commission's general arrogance towards the member states. all this behaviour has a common cause: the commission believes that it alone holds a superior truth. unfortunately, the draft european constitution reinforces this idea, whereas it should clearly be made a subordinate body.
in writing. - while we can only agree with the condemnation of the concept of 'ivory' and the murders committed in its name, we did not vote for this report. on the one hand, it conceals the responsibility of successive french governments which, after a long period of colonial oppression, supported the dictatorship of houphouët-boigny, and then the authoritarian regime of his successor bédié, who invented the demagogy of "ivoirité" in his struggle against his rivals for power. and, even today, the french army on the ground protects the interests of french capital in côte d'ivoire, and not the population. moreover, what does 'restoring the authority of the state' mean if it does not offer the means to end 'poverty, unequal distribution of wealth, social injustice, violations of human rights, oppression of minorities ...', which the report itself sees as so many destabilising factors that have led to the current conflicts? as for the so-called peacekeeping forces, such as those of ecowas, the precedents of sierra leone and liberia have shown that they are generally only adding an armed band to those already fighting on the backs of the population. we have not voted in favour of a hypocritical text which would only relieve the european parliamentarians of their conscience.
in writing. - the joint resolution is paternalistic from the outset, stating that the conflict in côte d'ivoire "cannot be attributed to the ethnic factor alone"... which nevertheless enhances the said factor. but is it not the neoliberalisation of the ivorian economy, the fall in the price of raw materials and thus the impoverishment of the population, the open competition of the ivorian neo-colonial factions by transnational firms, which have fostered the receptivity of the discourse of "liberty", and the coups d'état? the joint resolution does not mention the need for the withdrawal of french troops as a peacekeeping force. however, the historical relationship of the french army and companies with the ivorian political class and the neighbouring states means that the french army and diplomacy cannot be considered in a neutral position. other actors should therefore be promoted. the linas-marcoussis framework is therefore flawed in many respects. the best policy for preventing conflicts is to eradicate them from their foundations, and in this case arsonists cannot be good firefighters. we must get out of a deeply anti-democratic neocolonial logic and move towards a different form of cooperation between europe and africa. i therefore abstained on a resolution which does not take these problems head on.
in writing. - once again, our parliament has just adopted a mediocre resolution on the ivory coast debacle, failing to distinguish between its causes and its essential and incidental aspects. the bottom line is that a set of ethnically based forces openly racist (intertribal, anti-white, anti-french) are squandering their legacy of stability and prosperity. the abuses committed in the past fortnight in abidjan by militiamen who claim to be 'patriots' against representatives of humanitarian ngos who are doing a remarkable job, particularly in the service of children and diplomatic representatives, are all the more scandalous and unacceptable because they are taking place with complete impunity and under the complacent eye of the police. the double-dealing of the government authorities must be clearly denounced. these demonstrations are not spontaneous. they are organized in secret by president gbagbo and his entourage, whose art of double-talk reaches the heights. the "young patriots" are armed, funded and exploited by a legitimate government that betrays its function. in the face of the scale of such abuses, france and the european union must urgently adopt a firm stance and establish a clear link between aid and respect for rights, unless they give the impression that they are complacent or complicit.

(fi) mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, road tolls are never popular, especially if you have to pay them yourself, but they are a fact of life in europe today. they are necessary. the question is only how we can minimize the harm and the cost of them. the commission has already taken a number of measures to improve the quality of the services provided by the public authorities. it is clear that to avoid problems they must be harmonized. the excellent objective of this commission proposal is that each individual should have only one contract and that each vehicle should have only one device, so that the internal market would work well. this is just plain common sense. i agree with mrs sommer that interoperability is the goal, not the means to achieve it. i would disagree with the commission a little: i think we need more room for manoeuvre for local authorities, because this will prevent the already good and functioning systems from being scrapped simply because we are moving too quickly to a satellite system. the objective is to ensure that the systems work well together, not to determine whether they operate on microwaves or on some other wavelength. it is therefore sufficient to lay down general requirements to achieve the basic objective of the directive, namely the interoperability of systems. it's the key. a dynamic europe needs road transport. a prosperous europe needs mobility. as good as it is that we are standardising these systems, we must also be careful to ensure that costs are kept within reasonable limits and that we do not voluntarily take the straitjacket.

- mr president, madam commissioner, we shall naturally vote for this regulation. we believe that we have reached a text which is fairly well balanced in relation to an initial proposal which we felt presented a number of dangers. clearly, the right of the passengers is a sacred right. however, airlines often treat it very lightly, whether in terms of handling or passenger information. it is also clear that the practice of over-reservation has, in many cases, shown its limits and is being used as a commercial tool. we have even seen planes that did not take off because they were not full, which is absolutely unacceptable for someone who signed a contract of sale or purchase in the context of obtaining a ticket. i think that the text we have produced is overall balanced. on the one hand, it seeks to ensure that the practice of over-reservation is not a purely commercial practice but is limited to a practice of flexibility. overbooking, we know that it will never be reduced to zero in airlines, because that's how they handle overweight people. there are a number of us in this room who fly very often. however, many of us also take advantage of overbooking practices when we arrive late or when things go wrong and there are traffic jams to access the airport. i therefore believe that it is important not to make demagoguery in this respect. secondly, the compensation system must be fair and equitable, not too complicated to avoid endless litigation and, above all, not an incentive for airlines to take safety risks. we must not go too far and say that airlines will not say: i will leave at any cost, even if i have a technical incident, because it will cost me too much to compensate passengers. i hope that we have reached that balance in the context of this report. i wish i could, but i'm not sure. we will, however, give him our support.

- mr president, given the scale of the various problems posed by gmos, on which no obvious scientific conclusion is necessary, the question of the coexistence of the gmo and non-gmo sectors must be considered in a sustainable way and not as a transitional situation to be managed while waiting for the gmo sector to become the dominant or even exclusive sector. it is traditional and organic farming that is the common law and gmos the exception under observation, not the other way around. the question is not whether non-gmo sectors are feasible, but how to prevent the gmo sectors from contaminating the other sectors. the rapporteur is right to point out that we have a proven lack of knowledge in a number of crucial areas, which should encourage us to continue our research but also to be very cautious. these are allofertilisation, seed winter storage, soil concentration, resistance, diffusion and dissemination. we must be very careful that the provisions adopted on authorization, traceability and labelling are not bypassed by provisions which are too vague, uncertain or unclear on coexistence, thus creating a fait accompli which would sweep away all these precautionary measures. we must be careful not to put our farmers in the position of apprentice sorcerers to whom public opinion would inevitably attribute the negative consequences of the widespread dissemination of gmos. they had a big breakfast with the animal flours and the gaucho. so let us not make the maintenance of traditional production so complex that farmers are forced to abandon them in favour of gmos. the person who introduces a risk culture bears all the consequences of this risk. it is the one who takes the risk of contamination who must bear the costs of prevention and management of this risk vis-à-vis the other crops and their users and assume sole responsibility for it. the question of controlling the cohabitation of the sectors will become a central question of spatial planning. specific guidelines must be freely chosen at national or regional level. if, for example, elected representatives, farmers and other local actors in a territory want it to be free of gmos, they must be able to decide freely, without the commission being able to impede this in the name of some more or less imaginary distortion of competition. we shall therefore vote in favour of this own-initiative report, which asks the right questions on a vital social issue.

in writing. - i voted against the sommer report because the proposal to set up a european telenetwork system goes too far. the white paper's objective of tackling road congestion could be achieved by other means. european telephony is not a priority in this area. for example, it would be more sensible to reduce heavy goods traffic by encouraging the use of rail. the adaptation of member states' infrastructures for the establishment of such a system would entail disproportionate costs which would again be passed on to users. the current toll systems work relatively well and there is no urgency to implement such a system. in the name of the principle of subsidiarity, the choice of a particular toll system and the appropriate technology should be left to the discretion of the member states.
in writing. - the european council, held in brussels on 12 and 13 december, marked the end of the last full presidency before the european elections and opened a period of 'end of mandate' for parliament and the commission. the end of this mandate was marked by a shortness of breath among the institutions, with the blocking of the constitutional draft - see, in this connection, my explanation of vote on the igc results - the commission's inability to take back control after being shaken by successive scandals - see, in this connection, my explanation of vote on the commission's 2004 work programme - but also with two very revealing conclusions of the brussels council. first, the decision to announce a major programme of work, called 'fast-start', without any understanding of how it will be financed. secondly, there is concern about the almost total lack of follow-up by the member states to the lisbon strategy, which was originally designed to strengthen the competitiveness of the european economy. the impression is that the european system is running at a dead end, with the member states having little more than display objectives. is it not an inevitable return to the stick, the result of an excessive will to do everything, to dominate everything?
in writing. - this joint resolution is a mixture of "good feelings", hypocritical in terms of human rights, and the usual diplomatic and commercial cynicism of the great powers. does china not respect human rights? no, of course, like the dozens and dozens of states and despicable dictatorships to which the european union has sold, sells and will sell arms, to oppress their peoples or to take it out on their neighbours and to fatten the western gun dealers. from saddam hussein's iraq, armed by france, britain, germany, russia and the united states, to israel, to the dictatorships of latin america, asia, africa and elsewhere, no embargo has ever stopped arms companies, especially european ones. they are all the more able to circumvent such embargoes - in china as elsewhere - because they have the active complicity of european governments.
in writing. - i fully support the conclusions of the graefe zu baringdorf report and those of my colleague, mr souchet, in his speech yesterday on the coexistence of gm and non-gm crops. this is a major problem, which cannot be ignored by immediately granting authorisations for the cultivation and marketing of gmos, as the commission would have wished. the risks of contamination of traditional crops, which 70% of consumers want to preserve at least, should be carefully studied first. the second is to establish (if possible) prudent coexistence rules, and to place the responsibilities and costs of introducing gmos on the businesses that have been granted authorisations. finally, provision should be made for financial guarantees to cover these liabilities. but none of this is clear today. it is therefore disgusting to see the commission ready to give authorisations, using the pretext of subsidiarity to place on the states the almost impossible task of establishing the rules of coexistence, and at the same time prohibiting those states from declaring certain regional areas free of gmos (commission decision of 2 september 2003 v austria). this matter is being handled with intolerable contempt for the citizens.
in writing. - the rapporteur proposes a strict separation between traditional crops and gm crops. he is very biased, since he himself practices what is known as organic farming. nevertheless, the separation he proposes has at least the advantage of leaving choice to consumers. there is no need to share its anti-scientific attitude, which consists in making science say what it does not say, in order to approve a delimitation which allows a field of experimentation and verification to be reserved for research in the gmo sector, while taking care not to mix the sectors. the precautionary principle applies not so much to researchers as to the large capitalist groups - in this case, the seed companies and the agri-food giants - for whom scientific advances are a means of increasing their profits. where profit is the priority, irresponsibility is always the one that risks prevailing, with disastrous consequences for humans and nature.
in writing. - i am pleased with the positive reception given by parliament to the graefe zu baringdorf report, but surprised by the vote of members, particularly french ones, in favour of the dissemination of new varieties of gmos before the establishment of binding rules on coexistence. it is true that the ambition of seed companies which have invested heavily in research and development of genetically modified varieties is very logical to obtain the maximum return on investment as soon as possible. they therefore naturally tend to support the idea that a new generation of seeds will inevitably become widespread and will quickly replace improved seeds without genetic modification, as if it were a phenomenon analogous to the replacement of mechanical traction by animal traction. such a shift towards the standardization of seeds - all-gmo - and the corresponding disappearance of traditional and organic production channels would call into question the agricultural diversity of our european territories and therefore the specificity of the products derived from them. the fight for agricultural diversity, for the effective and sustainable plurality of sectors, is therefore an integral and essential part of the fight for cultural diversity.
the commission is therefore proposing that the commission should be given the task of drawing up a report on the situation in the south of france. my colleague, michel barnier, was unfortunately unable to come to strasbourg today. as you know, the question of natural disasters was discussed at length here on 1 september, after a hot summer. the commission has been actively working on the issue of natural disasters in recent years, in close cooperation with the european parliament. in the face of disasters that seem to be accelerating, two key words underpin the commission's actions: reparation and prevention. when it comes to reparations, it is a question of solidarity. following the floods in austria, the czech republic and germany in the summer of 2002, the commission, at the initiative of mr barnier, proposed the creation of the solidarity fund. thanks to the support of your assembly and the council, this new instrument has now been in operation for a year and has been called upon 14 times since its creation; it has been effective in eight cases. at present, the commission does not yet have sufficient information on the recent floods in southern france to be able to say whether the fund can be mobilised. in any event, we can only act on the official request of the french national authorities. if we receive a request, we will examine it as soon as possible. be assured that we will take account of the situation in the south of france in the evaluation we will make at the conference organised by the european commission on 5 march 2004. the purpose of this conference is to take stock of the use of the solidarity fund by several regions of europe. i should also point out that the regions of languedoc-roussillon and paca already receive substantial assistance from the european union under objective 2 of the structural funds. for the period 2000-06, this aid amounts to eur 316 million for languedoc-roussillon and eur 340 million for the paca region. during the floods that affected these regions in september 2002, specific measures were taken to compensate for the losses suffered. the mid-term review provides an opportunity to re-emphasise preventive or remedial actions. in the likely event that the regions concerned benefit from the allocation of the performance reserve and in the event of a good performance of the programmes in question, this could represent an additional approximately 4% of their allocation, i.e. eur 10.8 million for languedoc-roussillon and eur 12.3 million for the paca region. the french government will propose the allocation to the commission before 31 december next. important measures in the context of regional development may be financed. let me now turn to the second keyword: we must not only fix things, we must also give priority to prevention. these natural disasters raise the fundamental question of climate change and prevention for which research is needed. you can be assured of my commitment, and that of mrs wallström and the commission as a whole, in this area. as michel barnier recently told your committee on regional policy, he intends to propose the inclusion of a heading on 'natural hazard prevention' in each structural fund programme for the next programming period. in the same vein, the third report on economic and social cohesion, which will be adopted by the commission early next year, will propose that risk prevention be part of the objectives of the structural funds in the next programming period, beyond 2006. in addition, the commission is considering strengthening european civil protection coordination, including through the creation of a joint european civil protection force, an idea to which michel barnier is particularly attached and on which he is working closely with ms wallström. this new initiative, which is due to start early next year, should build on existing structures by equipping them with the necessary means to respond quickly and promptly to any type of disaster.
- mr president, commissioner, flooded streets, mud-covered houses, deteriorating networks, desperate populations: are we destined to become accustomed to these images of disasters which unfortunately recur every year? we are concerned about the severity of these floods, which unfortunately are recurrent. i would like to express our deep sympathy to all the victims, but also our gratitude to the civil security services and volunteers who have shown extraordinary dedication. the good coordination of the rescue services and european mutual aid, which has been able to make a real difference, can only be welcomed. our parliament has been very active in this area in calling for this mutual assistance to be put in place. once again, in this house, we must intervene in these natural disasters, the consequences of which could be better controlled. temporary shutdown, immediate restoration of the networks, temporary relocation, all this is just repair. it is well known that the cost of repair is much higher than the cost of prevention. prevention requires political courage and requires control of urban planning and coherent spatial planning. prevention is cheaper than repair, but you still have to be able to demand resources. it is true that at european level - as you reminded us, commissioner - the use of the structural funds is one of the good solutions for rebuilding dikes, strengthening them, simply maintaining watercourses, creating reservoirs. this structural fund policy has two limitations, however. the first is that the structural funds currently comply with the zoning rule and therefore do not place all victims on an equal footing. the second is that the amount of these funds is sometimes not sufficient. i would like to take my own region, the rhône-alpes region, as an example, which unfortunately is not mentioned today, although it was hit hard along with the provence-alpes-côte d'azur region and languedoc-roussillon. it has been in disaster recently, but will no longer be able to use the structural funds for the period 2003-06: everything has been spent. i am addressing my colleagues in this house who are sometimes tempted to cut or reduce the budget for regional policy. i say to them, beware, do not be deceived. these are the funds that most closely touch our fellow citizens, those that reflect the european solidarity which is the foundation of the union. we must all support commissioner barnier in his proposal to overhaul the structural funds. commissioner, you told us yourself. in future, these funds should no longer be based on zoning but should correspond to specific objectives, one of which would be environmental and risk prevention. in the face of the changes taking place on our planet, we need collective courage to meet these ecological challenges. i hope that the commission as a whole will follow commissioner barnier's proposals and that our parliament will be able to vote on the budget for the structural funds. in the meantime, we must make amends for the families who were killed. europe had already set up a solidarity fund for regions and states affected by natural disasters. it must also pool prevention technologies, building on successful experiences, such as in the netherlands, and setting up cross-border cooperation. i hope, mr president, commissioner, that we will not have any more debates on these natural disasters in the future.
- mr president, commissioner, my colleague has just said that she really wishes that in the future we would not have to add our tears to the waters that regularly devastate our regions. i'm not as optimistic as she is. i am much less optimistic, because i know very well that it was a wish you were making, mrs grossetête. however, we cannot be satisfied with wishful thinking when we see the climate change that is taking place on our planet. i was in my region of languedoc a few days ago and i was told that what we are experiencing now has never been seen before in the world. we've now met him three times in two years. so you can see that there is a change in frequency, amplitude and scale. i am always surprised to see the authorities, not just in my country, it would be too easy, but in all the countries that have been affected, running a little bit after the disaster. this summer, in the affected areas of southeastern france, people were already piling up sandbags. how come the locals knew, and the authorities rushed after the disaster? it is clear that there is a gap between those who are on the ground and who are suffering the destruction and the decision-makers, who are obviously still far away. the climate changes, with heat waves, storms and sudden rises in water. i don't feel that public policies change at the same rate. i think we would need to take a whole arsenal of measures to deal with this, including taxation. how many times have we in this house, the greens and the regionalists, said that we must certainly use the tax weapon to change behaviour that is dangerous for the climate? and we are still waiting for this tax on pollution, this tax on emissions that are changing the atmosphere of our planet and that are ultimately destroying entire regions. aid is evolving. i understand, commissioner, that we have actually been implementing, step by step, disaster by disaster, financial elements for repair and prevention. my colleagues used to say that repairing is good, but preventing is better. however, prevention - and i agree with them on this point - is not conceivable without a thoroughgoing reform of the structural funds. as long as there's zoning, it's not going to work. understand that storms and floods often ignore the areas we have wisely marked off the ground, on a map, in brussels or elsewhere. it is therefore obvious that these funds must be reformed and perhaps all those structural funds which are not being used on the ground, but are being reimbursed to the community and then to the national budgets, could be better used for prevention in order to cope with this climate. in conclusion, i would say that these problems have clearly changed in frequency and scale. i do not feel that european public policies, even though they are changing - i take note of this and welcome it - are changing with the same speed and the same scale, and i regret it.

the south of france has just been struck by an unprecedented natural disaster. today we are beginning to measure the extent of the damage, which is considerable. seven people have died and nearly 100,000 are estimated to be affected. tens of thousands of people had to take refuge in gymnasiums or in makeshift housing. in the city of arles alone, a third of the population was evacuated. thousands of jobs have been lost to the flood. hundreds of flooded businesses have had to close their doors, plunging their employees into the uncertainty of technical unemployment. the camargue, whose ecosystem is so fragile, is completely submerged: 250 km of damaged dikes, 560 hectares of crops covered by water, more than 1000 animals drowned, the entire rice chain destroyed. the damage suffered by the region will exceed €1 billion. european solidarity must be expressed in accordance with article 2 of the regulation establishing the solidarity fund. this is an exceptional disaster, the region having been hit by the "centennial crust" of the rhone, the worst of the century. on behalf of the french socialists, i ask that the european union quickly release these funds. the people of the rhône delta are waiting for this gesture.

commission. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the problem of transnistria has been a long-standing concern of the european union. in the declaration made at the recent osce ministerial summit in maastricht, in which the commission fully participates, the eu presidency reaffirmed our commitment to safeguard the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the republic of moldova. it confirmed its full support for the five-party negotiating framework comprising the osce, the russian federation, ukraine and the two parties concerned. the european union considers that this framework constitutes an appropriate transparent forum for finding a political solution to the conflict. in maastricht, the european union expressed its disappointment at the lack of progress in fulfilling the commitments made by russia in istanbul in 1999, namely the withdrawal of its troops and munitions from transnistria. the european union called on russia to honour its commitments. it considers that only a truly multinational commitment will have international legitimacy and reiterated its willingness to help find a multinational solution under the osce umbrella. the european union is also taking concrete action to promote a settlement of the conflict. the commission and moldova are finalising the drafting of an agreement establishing a double-checking system for steel exports from moldova to the european union. this system will strengthen moldova's control over exports from the breakaway region. the commission also encourages moldova to improve control of its borders and customs territory. in march 2003, the commission organised a first meeting between moldova and ukraine to consider the introduction of joint controls along their common borders and to discuss bilateral issues. a second meeting will be held in january 2004. the 'enlarged europe - a new neighbourhood' initiative opens up new prospects for extending to moldova the stability, security and prosperity that we have established within the enlarged european union. the very clear european perspective offered to moldova in the framework of the 'enlarged europe' initiative will, we hope, act as an additional incentive to reach a settlement of the conflict in transnistria. the commission will continue to monitor developments and will continue to address the issue of compliance with the istanbul commitments with the russian federation.
